title: Two architectures on one chip: Arm and IBM team up in a legendary crossover, but alas it's for 'enterprise infrastructure'
summary: It will reportedly operate at more than 5.7 GHz.
body: Though us PC gamers are unlikely to get the benefit of it, sometimes some new bit of PC hardware comes out of the enterprise market that just makes you go 'huh, that's neat'. Today, it's a new chip from IBM made in collaboration with Arm that runs architectures from both companies on a single chip. That means it will be able to run Arm-based Linux environments as well as IBM's z/OS, and the software that comes with both. Prior to this, running multiple sets of instructions would require emulating the right instructions, ie, turning instructions from one architecture to another that can actually be processed by the cores. Though we won't know how well it runs in use until the chip actually launches, it's still an interesting bit of tech that could be more versatile long-term. Combining two different architectures in one chip is very uncommon, though not unprecedented. title: Be Quiet! Light Mount TKL review
summary: A very welcome TKL update that didn't quite leave me speechless.
body: My prime PC gaming hours tend to be when the rest of my household is already in bed. As such, the fantastically clicky-clacky key presses of a mechanical gaming keyboard echoing through our halls isn't really ideal. It's just as well then that Be Quiet! is back with a welcome update to the very nearly silent keyboard I loved last year, the Light Mount . As someone with a perennially messy desk, the Light Mount TKL's 80% size is just right; I have room to swish my mouse, and I find I'm not forever accidentally hitting the capslock key as with other cut-down keebs. This TKL update offers more than just a smaller form factor, though, introducing the next generation of Be Quiet!'s Silent switches in Linear and Tactile flavours. This TKL update also addresses one of the key problems I had with the original Light Mount by introducing new gaming features. This includes Quick Tap (SOCD), which will be sweet percussion to the ears of shooter fans—and at best eyebrow raising for the esports sickos. body: ماذا حدث؟ خيّم الحزن على نادي بيراميدز بعد وفاة اللواء هشام زيد، مدير إدارة المباريات بالنادي، اليوم الثلاثاء، عقب تعرضه لأزمة صحية مفاجئة خلال الأيام الماضية، نقل على إثرها إلى أحد مستشفيات القاهرة الجديدة قبل أن يفارق الحياة. ونعى مجلس إدارة نادي بيراميدز واللجنة التنفيذية وجميع العاملين بالنادي، اللواء الراحل، معربين عن خالص حزنهم لوفاته، ومقدمين العزاء إلى أسرته وذويه، سائلين المولى عز وجل أن يتغمده بواسع رحمته. وأكد النادي أن هشام زيد كان من الكفاءات المشهود لها بالإخلاص والتفاني في العمل، وقدم الكثير لبيراميدز خلال السنوات التي تولى فيها مسؤولية إدارة المباريات، وكان له دور بارز في تنظيم وإدارة مباريات الفريق. وتقدم بيراميدز بخالص العزاء إلى أسرة الفقيد، داعيًا الله أن يسكنه فسيح جناته، وأن يلهم أهله الصبر والسلوان، في أعقاب رحيله الذي خلف حالة من الحزن داخل النادي. وأعلن النادي أن صلاة الجنازة على اللواء هشام زيد ستقام عصر اليوم على أن يوارى جثمانه الثرى في مقابر العائلة.

title: كومباني يغازل نجم بوروسيا دورتموند الجديد

title: بن سبعيني يدفع ثمن واقعة الصيباري

title: ضربة جديدة لبرشلونة.. تحرك إنجليزي يهدد بديل ألفاريز
summary: ماذا يفعل النادي الكتالوني؟
body: ماذا يفعل النادي الكتالوني؟ دخل نوتنجهام فورست على خط التعاقد مع الكولومبي لويس سواريز، مهاجم سبورتينج لشبونة، بعدما بدأ النادي الإنجليزي تحركاته لضم اللاعب، في وقت ارتبط فيه اسمه خلال الأيام الماضية باهتمام برشلونة. كان سواريز قد ظهر ضمن الخيارات المحتملة أمام برشلونة لتدعيم مركز المهاجم، في ظل بحث النادي الكتالوني عن بديل هجومي. ويبلغ سواريز28  عامًا، ويرتبط بعقد مع سبورتينج لشبونة حتى يونيو 2030، مع وجود شرط جزائي تبلغ قيمته80  مليون يورو، وفق موقع ترانسفير ماركت. كان المهاجم الكولومبي، قد قدم موسمًا لافتًا مع سبورتينج، بعدما سجل38 هدفًا خلال الموسم الماضي، ليؤكد مكانته كأحد أبرز المهاجمين في الدوري البرتغالي، ويجذب اهتمام أندية أوروبية عدة. ويأتي تحرك نوتنحهام فورست في وقت حساس من سوق الانتقالات، إذ يسعى النادي الإنجليزي إلى استغلال الأيام الأخيرة لإتمام الصفقة، بينما سيكون سبورتينج أمام اختبار صعب إذا وصل عرض مالي كبير ومناسب للتخلي عن مهاجمه. وفي المقابل، لا يزال اسم سواريز حاضرًا في حسابات برشلونة كأحد الخيارات الهجومية المطروحة، لكن موقف النادي الكتالوني من الصفقة يبدو أقل وضوحًا مقارنة بالاهتمام المباشر من نوتنجهام فورست.

title: A disturbing '90s point-and-click horror game about waking up in a rundown asylum with no recollection of who you are is getting a glow up in 2026
summary: Sanitarium probably doesn't need a new version, but it's getting one anyway.
body: 1998 was a vintage year for PC gaming: Half-Life, Unreal, StarCraft, Thief and Baldur's Gate all released in lavish oversize retail boxes, and it was just as busy in console land: Ocarina of Time and Banjo-Kazooie released on Nintendo 64, while the original PlayStation enjoyed Metal Gear Solid and Resident Evil 2. Into this crowd of future classics was also Sanitarium, which shuffled onto shelves, probably sheepishly, in April 1998. It's an isometric point-and-click adventure starring Max, an amnesiac who wakes in a bizarre, rundown sanitarium. Lest you think this is a game about exploring a slightly eerie rundown hospital, let me disabuse you of that notion immediately: For fear of spoiling everything, I can only say: this game goes places. Richard Cobbett wrote about Sanitarium in his Crapshoot column , and Alexis Ong even went as far as to track down its creators . If you've played Sanitarium—especially divorced from its mid '90s context—you're probably evangelical about it. It carefully balances the line between camp and psychologically gruelling, but questions of tone aside, it's a gorgeously vivid and varied thing, with beautifully rendered isometric environments. title: Nearly 500k players showed up for the Wardogs beta: 'The reaction from the FPS community has been insane'
summary: That's a big beta for such a complex FPS.
body: You ever get the feeling that a game is about to make a big splash, but nobody you know is talking about it yet? That's where I've been with Wardogs , the 100-player milsim FPS that I haven't stopped thinking about for weeks . Wardogs has steadily built buzz over the past year, recently eclipsing a million wishlists. Developer Bulkhead held a closed beta this past weekend for those who pre-ordered the $40 early access release, which reached over 100,000 peak Steam players on Sunday—more simultaneous players than Squad, Hell Let Loose, or Arma has ever seen on PC. In a beta debrief video published today, game director Howard Philpott said nearly 500,000 total players tried Wardogs. "The reaction from the FPS community has been insane," Philpott said, "with nearly half a million unique players showing up to play the closed beta the same week as Call of Duty's beta and Battlefield 6's massive update." title: A game dev spent 40 days in the wilderness to make this new Steam survival game

body: I've always wondered how I'd fare in a survival situation. Lost in the woods, with no food or water, how long would I last? Would I make good choices? Could I find my way back to safety? The answers to those questions are almost certainly "Not long, no, and definitely not," and hopefully I'll never have to actually find out. In the meantime, I try to live out my survival fantasies through films and games, and Wordless Forest, which launched on Steam today, is sorta both. Wordless Forest is an FMV survival game solo developer Dogus Cagrici shot while hiking in the "dense forests and wilderness of four different cities across Turkey for 40 days ." It's completely dialogue-free (hence the title) as the character Cagrici plays finds himself alone in the wilds, trying to find his way to safety and put his scrambled memories back together after a head injury. As the survivor attempts to make his way to a distant firewatch tower, you'll have to make choices for him. There's some food at an abandoned campsite that may be unsafe to eat: should you risk it? To be fair, the network test wasn't built to make a great first impression. It was limited to one map, six playable characters, no build customization, solo queue only, and seemed to only have a portion of its intro tutorial. body: A couple weeks back I noted that I'd been tracking GPU prices on an almost weekly basis for a year now, and that things have never been worse . Well, PC Partner—one of the biggest manufacturers of graphics cards you've probably never heard of—suggests it's going to get even worse. And probably quickly. PC Partner makes a ton of graphics cards for its consumer facing brands Zotac, Inno3D, and Manli. I've visited one of its main factories in Dongguan, China, and it's production lines are big. So when Singaporean outlet, The Straits Times , notes the company as saying that the supply of graphics cards is going to get real tight in the coming months it's worth listening. And the worst part about it is that apparently it's going to be the entry level cards that will be the most adversely affected. That's exactly what happened with Dishonored —the game that cemented Arkane's reputation as the new guardian of this particular strand of RPG.
